# Information Security Program Governance Standard

**Organization:** Example Org
**Owning Team:** Security Program / GRC
**Review Cadence:** Annual
**Governing Evidence Artifacts:** Approved policy set with review dates; Program plan and org chart

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard establishes the requirements for governing Example Org's information security program, including the development, maintenance, approval, dissemination, and protection of the organization-wide information security program plan, the risk management strategy, planning policies and procedures, system security and privacy plans, and the documentation required by the HIPAA Security Rule.

The Security Program / GRC team is accountable for this process end to end, including all reviews, updates, approvals coordination, dissemination, and evidence retention described in this Standard. Other teams participate in individual steps as identified, but the Security Program / GRC team owns the process and its handoffs.

This Standard applies to all organizational systems, all organizational entities, and all personnel or roles involved in information security planning and program governance at Example Org.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities

### 2.1 Senior Information Security Officer

Example Org must appoint a senior information security officer with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain an organization-wide information security program. [NIST 800-53 PM-2 | ARC-AMPE PM-2]

### 2.2 HIPAA Security Official

Example Org must identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by the HIPAA Security Rule for the covered entity or business associate. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(2)]

### 2.3 Planning Policy Official

Example Org must designate an organization-defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the planning policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 PL-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-1] The Security Program / GRC team shall record the designated official and ensure the designation is reflected in the Program plan and org chart.

### 2.4 Officials Responsible for System Plans and Planning Controls

Example Org must designate officials to be responsible for the development of system information security program plans, and must name these officials in the appropriate security and privacy documents. [ARC-AMPE PM-1]

Example Org must designate officials to be responsible for the management of planning controls for systems, must name these officials in the appropriate security and privacy documents, and must ensure planning policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the information on that system. [ARC-AMPE PL-1]

The Security Program / GRC team shall maintain the record of these designations as part of the Program plan and org chart.

## 3. Organization-Wide Information Security Program Plan

### 3.1 Development and Content

The Security Program / GRC team shall develop and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan that:

1. Provides an overview of the security program requirements and describes the program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting them;
1. Identifies and assigns roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance;
1. Reflects coordination among the organizational entities responsible for information security; and
1. Is approved by a senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk being incurred to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, and reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation. [NIST 800-53 PM-1 | ARC-AMPE PM-1]

The approved program plan constitutes the "Program plan and org chart" evidence artifact and must be retained by the Security Program / GRC team with its review dates.

### 3.2 Review and Update

The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the organization-wide information security program plan at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, which include:

- System architectural or design changes;
- Organization-wide assessment or audit findings;
- Security or privacy incidents or breaches; and
- Changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 PM-1 | ARC-AMPE PM-1]

### 3.3 Protection of the Program Plan

The organization-wide information security program plan must be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification. [NIST 800-53 PM-1 | ARC-AMPE PM-1] The Security Program / GRC team shall store and control access to the plan in the [Document Management System] such that disclosure and modification are restricted to authorized personnel.

### 3.4 Common Controls Documentation

Common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems must be documented in an appendix to the organization-wide information security program plan, unless they are described in a separate system security plan. The plan must indicate which separate security plans contain descriptions of common controls. [NIST 800-53 PM-1] The Security Program / GRC team shall maintain this appendix and the cross-references to separate security plans.

### 3.5 Monitoring of Legal and Regulatory Change

The Security Program / GRC team shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect information security program plans, and shall review the plans at least every one (1) year to ensure they remain effective. The plans must support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the information on that system. [ARC-AMPE PM-1]

## 4. Risk Management Strategy

### 4.1 Strategy Development

The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a comprehensive strategy to manage security risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation associated with the operation and use of organizational systems, and privacy risk to individuals resulting from the authorized processing of personally identifiable information. [NIST 800-53 PM-9 | ARC-AMPE PM-9]

### 4.2 Consistent Implementation

The risk management strategy must be implemented consistently across the organization. [NIST 800-53 PM-9 | ARC-AMPE PM-9]

### 4.3 Strategy Review and Update

The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the risk management strategy at least every one (1) year or as required, to address organizational changes. [NIST 800-53 PM-9 | ARC-AMPE PM-9]

## 5. Planning Policy and Procedures

### 5.1 Policy Development and Dissemination

The Security Program / GRC team shall develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel or roles an organization-level planning policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. The Security Program / GRC team shall also develop procedures to facilitate implementation of the planning policy and associated planning controls. [NIST 800-53 PL-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-1]

The planning policy, together with the other approved policies governed by this Standard, forms part of the "Approved policy set with review dates" evidence artifact maintained by the Security Program / GRC team.

### 5.2 Review and Update

The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the planning policy and the planning procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, which include:

- Assessment or audit findings;
- Security or privacy incidents; and
- Changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 PL-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-1]

## 6. System Security and Privacy Plans

### 6.1 Plan Content

Security and privacy plans must be developed for the system that:

1. Are consistent with the organization's enterprise architecture;
1. Explicitly define the constituent system components;
1. Describe the operational context in terms of mission and business processes;
1. Identify the individuals that fulfill system roles and responsibilities;
1. Identify the information types processed, stored, and transmitted;
1. Provide the security categorization with supporting rationale;
1. Describe specific threats of concern;
1. Provide the results of a privacy risk assessment for systems processing PII;
1. Describe the operational environment and any dependencies on or connections to other systems or components;
1. Provide an overview of the security and privacy requirements;
1. Identify any relevant control baselines or overlays;
1. Describe the controls in place or planned, including rationale for tailoring decisions;
1. Include risk determinations for security and privacy architecture and design decisions; and
1. Include security- and privacy-related activities requiring planning and coordination with organization-defined individuals or groups. [NIST 800-53 PL-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-2]

### 6.2 Template Conformance

The System Security and Privacy Plan must be consistent with the ARC-AMPE SSPP template. [ARC-AMPE PL-2]

### 6.3 Approval Prior to Implementation

The system security and privacy plans must be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to plan implementation. [NIST 800-53 PL-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-2] The Security Program / GRC team shall coordinate the approval and record it.

### 6.4 Distribution and Change Communication

Copies of the system security and privacy plans must be distributed, and subsequent changes to the plans must be communicated, to organization-defined personnel, roles, or stakeholders. [NIST 800-53 PL-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-2] The Security Program / GRC team shall perform and record this distribution and change communication.

### 6.5 Plan Review and Update

The system security and privacy plans must be reviewed at least every one (1) year or following significant changes, and must be updated to address changes to the system and environment of operation or problems identified during plan implementation or control assessments. [NIST 800-53 PL-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-2]

### 6.6 Protection of Plans

The system security and privacy plans must be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification. [NIST 800-53 PL-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE PL-2] The Security Program / GRC team shall store and control access to the plans in the [Document Management System] such that disclosure and modification are restricted to authorized personnel.

## 7. Security Violations and Risk Assessment (HIPAA)

### 7.1 Security Violation Controls

Example Org must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(i)]

### 7.2 Risk Analysis

Example Org must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity or business associate. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)]

### 7.3 Risk Reduction

Example Org must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and [Assignment: complete requirement text — source requirement truncated in input]. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B)]

## 8. HIPAA Policy Implementation and Documentation

### 8.1 Implementation of Policies and Procedures

Example Org must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements. Any changes to these policies and procedures must be documented and implemented in accordance with the Rule. [HIPAA 164.316(a)]

### 8.2 Written Form and Documentation of Actions

Example Org must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule in written (which may be electronic) form, and must maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by the Rule to be documented. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1)]

### 8.3 Retention

HIPAA Security Rule documentation must be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i)] The Security Program / GRC team shall manage retention of this documentation in the [Document Management System].

### 8.4 Availability

HIPAA Security Rule documentation must be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]

### 8.5 Periodic Review and Update

HIPAA Security Rule documentation must be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)] The Security Program / GRC team shall perform and record this review.

## 9. Evidence and Records

The Security Program / GRC team shall retain, as evidence of compliance with this Standard:

- The approved policy set with review dates, comprising the planning policy and the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule; and
- The Program plan and org chart, comprising the approved organization-wide information security program plan and the recorded role designations required by Section 2.

All review and update activities performed under this Standard shall be recorded with their dates so that the annual review obligations in Sections 3, 4, 5, and 6 can be demonstrated to an auditor.
